knn_k.why: Neighbours kept in the structure-restricted fuzzy relation. 1 is a single best neighbour (near-reflexive), 40 is a dense bank; 10 is the frozen baseline.

graph_sigma.why: Bandwidth of r=exp(-d/(2 sigma^2)); unit-norm representations give d in [0,4], so 0.1 keeps near-duplicates only and 2.0 is a broad neighbourhood. 0.5 is the frozen baseline.

risk_limit.why: Held-out Wilson risk ceiling of the alpha gate (stricter gate -> higher alpha -> fewer accepted positives). 0.1 is the frozen baseline.

curriculum_ramp_rounds.why: Rounds until the soft curriculum reaches full weight. 2 is very fast, 10 is the frozen baseline, 40 is slower than the 30-round MNIST horizon.

full_boundary_weight.why: Boundary KL weight as a multiple of the frozen per-task value (MNIST 0.1, HWF 0.2). 0.0 keeps the boundary set but removes its loss term, which is not the same as the no_boundary ablation.

curriculum_min_weight.why: Optional secondary curriculum knob: initial soft-curriculum weight (curriculum strength). Not swept by default; requires --factors curriculum_min_weight.

notes: One factor at a time: every arm changes exactly one frozen-v10 full parameter, and the baseline arm is retrained inside the same campaign.
The grid is predeclared and contains the frozen baseline value; arms are never added after inspecting results.
Stage A screens with the design seed (4); stage B re-runs the baseline plus an interesting subset with seeds 0-4 and is the only admissible confirmation.
Formal test is never read by this protocol; train.py only trains and selects on validation.
